title: High-throughput Protein Expression Generator Using a Microfluidic Platform
protocol: Purchase DTPA-D SU-8 control mold and SPR220-7 flow mold from Stanford Microfluidics Foundry.
Expose silicone molds to chlorotrimethylsilane (TMCS) vapor for 10 minutes.
Mix silicone-based elastomer and curing agent in a ratio of 5:1 for the control mold.
Mix silicone-based elastomer and curing agent in a ratio of 20:1 for the flow mold.
Pour the 5:1 PDMS mixture onto the control layer to a height of approximately 5 mm.
Degas the control layer thoroughly.
Bake the control layer at 80 °C for 30 minutes.
Spin coat the 20:1 PDMS mixture on the flow layer at 2,600 rpm for 60 seconds.
Bake the spin-coated flow layer at 80 °C for 30 minutes.
Separate the control layer from the mold slowly and carefully.
Cut the device around its perimeter.
Punch holes to access the control channels.
Align the flow and control layers manually under a stereoscope starting with the upper left corner.
Ensure that the button valve is in the middle of the reaction chamber.
Gently align and release each row of the control layer.
Check alignment of all button valves and address/input valves across the flow channels.
Carefully lift and release tension from the PDMS by lifting from sides and corners without causing misalignment.
Bake the device for 2 hours at 80°C.
Cut around the perimeter of the device after baking.
Peel the two-layer device (chip) from the flow mold.
Punch holes to access the flow channels.
Prepare a mixture of poly ethylene glycol (1.25%) and D-trehalose dihydrate (125 mg/ml).
Dispense 2 μl of the mixture per reaction into 384 wells plate.
Transfer synthetic genes to the 384 wells plate.
Add dH2O to a final volume of 20 μl for each well.
Spot a series of synthetic genes onto epoxy coated glass substrates using a microarrayer.
Use MicroGrid 610 (Bio Robotics) with SMT-S75 silicone pins (Parallel Synthesis, USA).
Contact print the DNA to form spots with a diameter of about 100 μm on the glass surface.
Ensure each pin load is sufficient for approximately 100 spots.
Make sure the column and row pitches correspond to the specific device used.
The device contains 16 columns and 40 rows with a pitch of 680 μm by 320 μm, respectively.
Manually align the microfluidic device to the gene array under a stereoscope.
Locate the first row of spots below the first row of DNA chambers.
Bring into line the rest of the rows, finishing with fine tuning of the whole device.
Lift locally to alleviate any stress in the PDMS.
Bond the device to the glass slide by overnight incubation on a hot plate at 80 °C.
Connect the device to the solenoid valves manifold using flexible plastic tubing and stainless steel pins.
Fill the tubes with deionized distilled water (DDW).
Insert the pin into the access holes of the control layer.
Ensure each tube is connected to its corresponding control channel.
Run the LabVIEW application on the computer to activate the control channels.
Set the air pressure to 5 psi.
Fill the 'sandwich' and address valves first.
Identify cross-talks between control channels of defective devices.
Increase the air pressure to 15 psi.
Activate valve control from a LabVIEW program through on/off switches connected to individual solenoid valves.
Connect a tube to one of the flow inputs and flow air into the device at 4-5 psi.
Load 40 μl of Biotinylated-BSA (1 μg/μl) in a new tube and flow approximately half of it for 20 min through the device.
Wash unreacted substrate with Hepes (50 mM) for 5 min.
Flow 25 μl Strepavidin (0.5 μg/μl) for 20 min on top of the biotinylated-BSA.
Wash with Hepes for 5 min.
Close the 'button' valve and flow the rest of the biotinylated-BSA (as described above).
Passivate the surface surrounding the button by washing with Hepes for 5 min.
Release the 'button' valve and flow 30 μl of penta-His-biotin (0.16 μg/μl) for 20 min.
Wash with Hepes for 5 min.
Express proteins on the device using rabbit reticulocyte quick coupled transcription and translation reaction.
Open the 'neck' valves and flow the reaction through the device into the DNA chamber.
Close the 'sandwich' valves to isolate each gene from its environment.
Incubate the device on a hot plate for 2.5 hr at 30 °C.
Label the expressed proteins with C-myc Cy3 antibody.
Determine protein expression levels with a microarray scanner using a 532 nm laser and 575 nm emission filter.
Create a graphic design for the device using AutoCAD based on experimental needs.
Print the design on a transparency film by a high-resolution image setter.
Expose the silicon wafer to contact photolithography using the transparency as a photomask.
Promote elastomer release after baking steps by exposing mold to chlorotrimethylsilane vapor for 10 min.
Prepare a mixture of silicone based elastomer and curing agent in a ratio of 5:1 for the control layer mold.
Degass and bake the control layer mold at 80 °C for 30 min.
Prepare a mixture of silicone based elastomer and curing agent in a ratio of 20:1 for the flow layer mold.
Spin coat the flow layer mold at 2,600 rpm for 60 sec and bake it at 80 °C for 30 min.
Separate the control layer from its mold and punch channel access holes.
Align the control and flow layers manually under a stereoscope.
Bake the aligned layers together at 80 °C for 2 hr.
Punch access holes in the flow channels of the two-layer device.
Express proteins on the device using a rabbit reticulocyte quick coupled transcription and translation reaction.
Load an expression mix (12.5 μl) into the device.
Flood the DNA chambers by opening the 'neck' valves.
Close the 'sandwich' valves to separate each unit cell from its neighbors.
Incubate the device on a hot plate for 2.5 hours at 30°C.
Allow proteins to diffuse through the gene chamber into the reaction chamber.
Bind the C-terminus His tag of expressed proteins to anti-His antibody localized under the 'button' valve.
Label proteins with a C-myc Cy3, which binds to its corresponding epitope located at the protein N-terminus.
Determine protein expression levels using a microarray scanner (LS Reloaded) with a 532 nm laser and 575 nm filter.
